plain_text:
1 | P a g e 
 
 City of Concord, NH   Recreation and Parks Advisory Committee  
Meeting Minutes from September 17, 2026 5:30pm Approved 
  
  
Committee Members:), Althea Barton (Ward 1), Robert Kleiner (Ward 2), Nick Kotkowski (Ward 6) Brian Sartorelli (Ward 7, 
Mary Miller, Chair (Ward 10), City Councilor Michele Horne, Deodonne Bhattarai (Ward 9) and City Councilor Nate Fennessy 
 
Absent: Zoey Murphy (Ward 5), Dhan Timsina, (8), Kenny Edwards (Merrimack Valley School District), Jim Figueira (Ward 
3), Sarah Beauregard (Ward 4), Barb Higgins (Concord School District) 
 
Staff Members: Laura Bryant Assistant Parks & Recreation Director and Matt Walsh, Deputy City Manager 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:37 p.m. by Chair Mary Miller. Per the request of Deputy City Manager Matt Walsh, Mary 
Miller changed the Agenda so item #3 would be first. 
 
New Business:  
 
1. City Wide Master Planning Citywide Visioning Open House 9/19/26: Matt Walsh spoke about the master plan 
project which will kick off with a visioning session this upcoming Saturday September 19th, 9:00-11:00am at the Capital 
Center for the Arts. The project falls under the Planning Board, the planning board will be creating a sub-committee 
made up of members from several other city committees including RPAC. If RPAC could nominate 2 members to 
participate in the subcommittee that would be most helpful. Once the subcommittee is created they will meet roughly 4 
times throughout the next 18 months with the consultants. Additionally, the consultants will meet with RPAC in its 
entirety twice during the process. For the project timeline or more information on coming public meetings please check 
the city website www.concordnh.gov  
 
 
2. City Council Referral: Volunteer Corp: Councilor Michele Horne spoke about her proposal to use volunteer to help 
save money across the city. However, she stated she was unsure why the program had been referred to RPAC as Parks & 
Recreation was already using volunteers quite a bit. In addition to the presentation Councilor Horne also mentioned 
having a place available on the website where someone might be able to find all volunteer opportunities across the city. 
Althea Barton spoke about the legal concern of filling existing jobs with volunteers, even when trying to cover a budget 
reduction it is not allowed. Althea as an avid volunteer herself also spoke to the concern of managing volunteers and that 
in the long run it could lead to more staffing issues. After a robust conversation and some questions about the exact law, 
Laura Bryant read the RSA for clarification. Laura agreed she could look into working with other city staff to try and 
create a central location for all volunteer opportunities to be listed. 
 
3. Council Referral: Fee for use a Rollins Park: RPAC reviewed the email that was sent by the park user requesting that 
information about how to request a few waivers be more transparent. Councilor Nate Fennessy share some history of 
fees for those that weren’t involved in the past. After quite a bit of discussion the following motion was made by 
Councilor Nate Fennessy Parks & Recreation staff should create a transparent waiver policy to be reviewed by RPAC 
and voted on as to whether or not to be presented to City Council, seconded by Mary and approved. 
5 minutes public input: 
No public attended
2 | P a g e 
 
 
Old Business: Laura Bryant gave quick update on the following:  
 
 Memorial Field Master plan – City Council will have a public hearing in October to approved the 600K for design. The 
final plan keeps everything in the same places for the most part, they are adding a multiuse turf field in the southwest 
corner 
 
 Bike Park Planning – City Council approved design of the bike park at Russell Martin Park as long as the group 
continues to fundraise 
 
 Skate Park at Kiwanis Park – still working toward the fundraising goals of 500K to match LWCF grant 
 
 Snow making at Beaver Meadow Golf Course – Nate Fennessy spoke to this. All water lines are in as well as all the 
electrical need to run the snow machines. 
 
 
Councilor Michele Horne brought up that the signs in multiple languages about the trash (at Keach Park) need to be in every 
park. Deodonne Bhattarai said they are up to high so kids cannot see them. 
 
Councilor Michele Horne also said to either get rid of all of the trash cans in the parks or give everyone trash cans. 
 
Motion was made by Mary Miller to end the meeting at 6:35pm, seconded by Robert Kleiner and approved.  
 
Next RPAC meeting scheduled for Thursday October15, 2026 at 5:30pm.  
Submitted by Laura S. Bryant, Assistant Parks & Recreation Director
